title: I Posted the Skate-Sharpener Hours After They Camped My Numbered Jig

parts.text: I stepped into bench one at 4:08 p.m. and tech Lars was already using my numbered jig. The board said: FIFTEEN MINUTES. JIGS STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was twenty-eight, pro-shop tech, holding a clipboard that listed our hollow. Lars shrugged. "Techs keep the wheel." I photographed the board, the booking, and his blades on my jig. Then I asked for the sharpener hours. At 4:12 the pro-shop desk pinged why Lars's blades sat on our jig. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The pro-shop desk can see Lars's blades on bench one during our hollow.

social.video_title: He camped my numbered skate jig — Part 1/2
social.description: Skate sharpener, a tech on my jig, a fifteen-minute clock he posted. I logged the blades. Would you have asked for the sharpener hours?

parts.text: Lars called it cross-grinds until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the jig still. The jig went back to my numbered drawer. Lars ran a slot of their own and told the next tech atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: TECHS DO NOT KEEP THE WHEEL. I keep our hollow on a labeled card. Lars brown-bags his blades. The bench finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Techs do not keep the wheel — Part 2/2
social.description: Sharpener hours, numbered jig, and a second line on the board. Were cross-grinds ever our hollow?
